title: Prototype and Object Pool
idea: Prototype creates a new object by copying a ready-made one. Object Pool keeps a fixed set of costly objects and lends them out instead of rebuilding them.
points: A prototype exposes a `copy()` method or copy constructor that returns a new twin.
A deep copy duplicates mutable fields; a shallow copy shares them with the original.
A pool hands out an idle object, or creates one while under its limit.
Callers must return borrowed objects with `release`, or the pool runs dry.

steps.caption: The pool starts empty with a limit of two. Nothing is created until someone asks.
First `acquire`: nothing is idle, so the pool creates `conn-1` and lends it.
Second `acquire` creates `conn-2`. The pool has now reached its limit.
Third `acquire`: nothing idle and no room to create, so it gets an empty `Optional`.
`release(a)` puts `conn-1` back on the idle stack. It is not destroyed.
The next `acquire` pops `conn-1` again. Reuse, not a third creation.

code.title: Prototype
code.caption: Copy a template invoice, then edit the copy. A shallow copy leaks edits into the template.

walk.text: A `private` constructor stores the list it is given, as is.
The factory method builds the original with its own mutable list.
`copy` makes a new list: a deep copy, safe to edit.
`shallowCopy` reuses the same list: the classic Prototype bug.
Editing the deep copy leaves the template alone.
Editing the shallow copy changes the template too.

code.title: Object Pool
code.caption: A two-slot connection pool. The fake `Connection` stands in for something costly to open. It is a single-threaded sketch; a pool shared by threads needs a lock or a concurrent queue.

walk.text: The pool tracks idle objects, its limit and how many it has made.
Lend an idle one first; create only under the limit; else refuse.
`release` returns the object to the idle stack for the next caller.
Two borrows succeed; the third is refused while both are out.
After a return, the next borrow gets the same object back.

pitfalls: Deep-copy every mutable field in a prototype; copying references shares state silently.
Prefer a copy constructor or `copy()` over `Cloneable`, whose `clone()` is shallow by default.
Release pooled objects in `finally`, and reset their state before lending them again.

quiz.q: What is the last line `ObjectPoolDemo` prints?
quiz.why: `release(a)` put `a` on the idle stack, and `acquire` pops idle objects before creating new ones. Only two were ever created.

takeaway: Prototype copies a ready object; Object Pool lends costly objects for reuse.
